learningObjective: State the semantics of a CUDA stream (an in-order queue of device work) and a CUDA event (a synchronization point recordable on a stream), and their role in a runtime.
stem: Which statement most accurately describes CUDA streams and events in the context of an ML runtime that overlaps kernel execution with data transfers?

options.text: A stream represents a physical hardware queue with a fixed one-to-one binding to a specific SM group; events are per-SM performance counters that record occupancy and warp-stall statistics for later Nsight analysis.

A stream is an in-order queue of operations on the device — work enqueued on the same stream executes in order, work on different streams may execute concurrently; events are recorded on streams as synchronization markers that other streams (or the host) can wait on.

A stream is a mutable shared buffer that host and device both read/write; events are memory fences that flush the L2 cache to global memory before subsequent kernels begin executing on the same device.

Streams and events are optional debugging APIs whose only function is to expose timing information to profilers; kernel execution order is instead determined by the CUDA driver's global scheduler regardless of stream assignment.

explanation: A CUDA stream is an in-order queue of device operations. Operations within the same stream execute in issue order; operations across different streams may overlap (subject to hardware and driver policies). CUDA events are recorded on streams (`cudaEventRecord(event, stream)`) and act as synchronization markers — another stream can wait on the event, or the host can block until it completes. Overlapping copy-and-compute uses one stream for H2D and another for the kernel, synchronized by events.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: streams are logical queues, not physical SM bindings; events are not performance counters.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: matches the CUDA C++ Programming Guide description of streams and events.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: streams are not shared host/device buffers, and events are not L2 fences.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: streams determine execution order (within-stream in-order); they are not debug-only.

nonImplications: Does not imply cross-stream ops always run concurrently; concurrency depends on GPU resources and dependencies.
Does not imply events replace `cudaStreamSynchronize`; both are valid tools for different granularities.
